subject: ss-plastic-surgery
title: Congenital Hand Anomalies: Syndactyly, Polydactyly and Deficiency

steps.say: Fused webs, double thumbs, and short forearms are all landing in one classification system. The Oberg-Manske-Tonkin scheme is sorting anomalies into malformations, deformations, and dysplasias by their origin. Naming the correct category is guiding counselling about recurrence and associated syndromes.
steps.tx: The **Oberg-Manske-Tonkin (OMT) classification** system sorts congenital upper limb anomalies into **malformations** from abnormal formation, **deformations** from extrinsic forces, and **dysplasias** from faulty **cellular organization**. The category is predicting recurrence risk and pointing toward associated syndromes for workup. Getting the **category** right is guiding family counselling about recurrence and associated syndromes for workup.

steps.say: Fingers that never separated in the womb are presenting as a common webbed anomaly. Skin-only joining is defining simple syndactyly, while bone fusion is defining the complex form. Webbing reaching the fingertip is marking the complete variant that most needs release.
steps.tx: **Syndactyly** is failure of **digital separation**: **simple** joins skin only, **complex** fuses bone, **complete** reaches the fingertip, and incomplete stops short. The commonest congenital hand anomaly is limiting spread and growth. Classification is deciding the graft plan and the timing for release surgery.

steps.say: Web release is waiting until the hand grows large enough for grafting. Zigzag incisions on both volar and dorsal sides are opening the web around twelve to eighteen months. Full-thickness grafts are resurfacing the raw sides so straight scars cannot drag the web forward.
steps.tx: **Syndactyly release** around **12 to 18 months** uses **zigzag incisions** volar and dorsal with **full-thickness skin grafts**. Grafts resurface raw sides so scars cannot contract into **web creep**. Waiting until the toddler months lets the hand grow large enough for tension-free graft take.

steps.say: Operating both sides of one finger in a single sitting is threatening its blood supply. Adjacent web spaces such as the two borders of the middle finger are never released together. Staged operations months apart are keeping each digit perfused while both webs eventually open.
steps.tx: Releasing both webs around one digit in a single sitting is forbidden: operating the **adjacent web spaces** together strips the finger from both sides and invites **digital ischemia**. Staging the two sides months apart is keeping each **release** perfused and safe.

steps.say: A double thumb is splitting at different levels that one classification is capturing. Seven Wassel patterns are describing the split from tip to base. The bifid proximal phalanx of type four is appearing most often in clinic.
steps.tx: **Radial polydactyly** duplicates the thumb in **seven Wassel** patterns by split level. **Wassel Type IV** with a bifid **proximal phalanx** is the commonest duplicate thumb. Higher numbers mean more proximal splits with trickier tendon, joint, and nail-fold anatomy to rebuild.

steps.say: Two small half-thumbs are merging into one normal-width thumb in selected cases. Symmetrical central wedges from both duplicates are joining into a single digit by the Bilhaut-Cloquet method. Wassel one and two deformities with two hypoplastic parts are suiting this combining operation.
steps.tx: The **Bilhaut-Cloquet** procedure merges symmetrical central wedges of both duplicates into one normal-width thumb. It suits **Wassel I and II** deformities where both parts are hypoplastic. Outer halves join with shared nail and bone for a single stable digit that grows straight.

steps.say: A short forearm deviating toward the thumb side is signalling a missing radial column. VACTERL association, Holt-Oram cardiac defects, and Fanconi marrow failure are hiding behind radial longitudinal deficiency. Blood counts with cardiac imaging are preceding any reconstruction plan.
steps.tx: **Radial longitudinal deficiency** (radial club hand) associates with **VACTERL**, Holt-Oram, and **Fanconi anemia**. Baseline **hematological** and cardiac evaluation precedes any surgery. Marrow failure and septal defects kill more often than the limb difference itself, so blood and cardiac screening comes before any limb surgery is planned.

steps.say: Tight bands wrapping the limb in the womb are leaving ring constrictions and missing parts. Circumferential grooves with distal acrosyndactyly are marking the amniotic band sequence. The severest bands are amputating digits before birth and leaving small nubbins behind.
steps.tx: **Constriction ring syndrome** (**amniotic band** sequence) gives circumferential constrictions, **acrosyndactyly**, or intrauterine amputations. Bands wrap the limbs at random depths and tightness, so no two children look alike. Deep grooves need surgical release while nubbins from **amputations** take prosthetic fitting and planning instead.
